title: Egg Mayonnaise Sandwich
subtitle: Classic British egg mayo sandwich
excerpt: Hard-boiled eggs mashed with mayonnaise, a little mustard, and chives, piled generously between sliced white bread. The most popular sandwich filling in Britain.

recipe.sourceNotes: Egg mayonnaise has been a staple of British cafes, deli counters, and meal deals since the postwar period. It consistently ranks as one of the most popular sandwich fillings in Britain. The quality of the egg mayo is determined entirely by two things: properly cooked eggs (which means the yolks should be just set and not green around the edges) and a good ratio of egg to mayonnaise. Season confidently.

content.text: Place the eggs in cold water to begin, bring to a boil, then cook for 10 minutes for a fully set yolk with no grey ring. Transfer to cold water immediately to stop the cooking. The filling should be just mixed, not over-worked into a paste: leave some texture so it has something to bite.
Place the eggs in a small saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, then cook at a steady simmer for 10 minutes. Transfer to a bowl of cold water and leave until completely cool.
Peel the eggs and mash roughly in a bowl with a fork. Add the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, chives, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined but still chunky.
Pile generously onto 2 slices of bread. Add cress if using. Top with the remaining slices. Press gently and cut in half.
